name: Arnica oil
description: Arnica oil (CAS 8057-65-6 ), also known as arnica flower oil, is a botanical extract derived from Arnica montana flowers, typically prepared by macerating the plant material in a carrier oil. It is used in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations primarily for its skin-conditioning and surface-wetting properties. In topical cosmetic products, arnica oil is incorporated into creams, balms, and massage oils to deliver moisturizing and skin-softening effects. Sports and recovery product lines use it in muscle rubs and body gels where its wetting behavior supports even distribution across skin surfaces. Pharmaceutical manufacturers include it in semi-solid preparations such as ointments and medicated creams targeting external application. Hair care formulators also use it in scalp treatments and conditioning products where botanical-derived oils are preferred over synthetic alternatives. Arnica oil is supplied as a liquid, most commonly as a standardized macerate in a carrier oil such as sunflower or olive oil, with arnica flower content typically specified by percentage. Cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet different regulatory requirements. Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller quantities available for formulation development and testing. This ensures that manufacturers can scale production from initial laboratory trials to full-scale commercial manufacturing efficiently. The product meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency across batches. Suppliers provide comprehensive documentation including certificates of analysis and safety data sheets to support the integration of this botanical extract into diverse product lines.
